characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Field emission gun SEM (FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with EBSD system; Channel 5 post-processing software
characterization_methods.key_findings: Al-6 steel shows only austenite (no BCC ferrite), average austenite grain size 34.2 ± 1.1 μm, twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 45.3 %.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground and electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; 15° misorientation boundary definition; grain size by linear intercept method
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase distribution and grain size as a function of alloying content

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific, 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: No κ-carbides present in the Fe30Mn6Al1C (Al-6) steel; D_κ-carbides = 0.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 20 V and -20 °C; dark-field images/SAED taken along [001]γ
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize κ-carbide precipitation in the austenite matrix
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) - dark field imaging with SAED

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Initial strain rate 1.1×10^-3 s^-1 at ambient temperature; round specimen gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Obtain engineering stress-strain response and strain hardening rates

characterization_methods.key_findings: Al-6: Akv(-40 °C) = 354 ± 16 J, the highest of all designed compositions.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Test temperature -40 °C; V-notch perpendicular to rod axis

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mass density of the fabricated steel

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict alloy density from alloying content (mass%)
analytical_models.model_name: Density as a function of C, Mn, Al content
analytical_models.model_note: ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (mass%), Eqn. (3). General to the alloy series including Al-6.

computational_details.simulation_method: Linear least-squares regression of measured density vs alloying content
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Eqn. (3) gives 6.6 g/cm³ for Fe30Mn11Al1.0C, matching the experimental Table 1 value.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute maximum true stress (σ_TS) and fracture strength (σ_FS) from tensile data
analytical_models.model_name: Ultimate true strength / fracture true strength
analytical_models.model_note: σ_TS = σ_UTS(1+UE); σ_FS = σ_EF/(1−A), Eqns. (1) and (2). Computed values for Al-6: σ_TS = 1410 MPa, σ_FS = 2113 MPa.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical true-stress conversion from engineering stress-strain data

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: highest Charpy impact toughness at -40 °C among all designed low-density steels (354 J)

processing_steps.method: high-frequency vacuum induction melting and casting into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace with a 50 kg capacity, then cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm.
Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, then air-cooled to room temperature (parent process proc_hot-rolled).
Hot-rolled rods were solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this defines the sample state (state_label 1050 °C–2 h–WQ).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Solution-treated specimen (1050 °C/2 h/WQ); engineering stress-strain response and strain hardening rate obtained by tensile test on an MTS machine; two solution-treated specimens tested and data reported as average of two specimens.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to rod axis

strain_hardening_rate.direction: maximum work hardening rate of 6% Al steel

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of Fe30Mn(x)Al1C with 6% Al after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment (Fig. 2(c)); true stress-strain and work hardening rate curves (Fig. 8(c))

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Measured using an MTS impact tester (500 J capacity); two solution-treated specimens tested, data average of two specimens.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Charpy impact specimen 55 mm long, 10×10 mm cross-section with a 2 mm deep V-notch; V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Experimental density measurement of the as-fabricated steel.

phases_present.volume_fraction: single-phase austenite (no ferrite reported; f_Bcc = '-' in Table 3)

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase FCC austenite with annealing twin boundaries after solution treatment at 1050 °C/2 h/WQ; no ferrite and no κ-carbides (the Fe1C30Mn6Al alloy does not contain κ-carbides, D_κ-carbides = 0).

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the Al-6 (Fe30Mn6Al1C) steel: C 0.99, Mn 29.48, Al 5.98, Fe Bal. (mass%), and measured density 7.12 g/cm³ (Table 1), the highest density/lowest Al member of the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series.
For Al-6, the maximum true stress just before necking (σ_TS) is 1410 MPa and the fracture strength (σ_FS) is 2113 MPa (Table 2).
In addition to the Table 3 value of 34.2 ± 1.1 μm, the text separately reports an austenite grain size of 33.4 μm for the 6% Al steel (not shown in Fig. 5).
The Fe1C30Mn6Al (Al-6) alloy does not contain κ-carbides, and its yield strength (433 MPa) and impact toughness (354 J) are the lowest-strength/highest-toughness endpoints of the Al-alloyed series.
Work hardening rate of the 6% Al steel shows a maximum of around 2100 MPa; the work hardening rate increases with decreasing Al content (Fig. 8(c)).
